doc.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014

title: Rap, abstract art and every generation's music
summary: Heath says music without melody and harmony is not music to him, recalls Percy's prediction about rap, and jokes about 'abscess' art.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: I played the record once and I was done with it. And even Mingus, I heard he said the same thing, it sounded like everybody in the practice room warming up to go on the stage. There’s no distinctive melody there. And what is music? Now we’ve got music that is words and a rhythm and no melody and no harmony. And that is not music to me. It’s music by the kids. They think it’s music. Every generation has their time. My brother went to his death, Percy, told me, “Aww that ain’t gonna last.” I say, “Yes it is Percy.” Just like I was listening to Glenn Miller on the TV last night. Because I heard that when I was a kid. They were trying to get money on PBS. So they were playing the big band era. So then they were playing the Four Brothers, then they played Lionel Hampton “Flying Home.” You know. Because I heard that when I was a kid so it’s going to be with you. You may be educated enough to leave that and go to something else, but you’re still going to remember that. Because you were raised up with that. So that’s what I was telling Percy man. Rap, they’re still going. He’s been dead since 2005. And that’s —

Yeah that music, or whatever they call it. But you know the artistic world now, through all the arts, paintings, music and everything, abscess paintings, abscess music. They call it abstract. I call it abscess. I’m done. And I’m done stepped on a lot of people’s toes and I’ve said enough. This is my opinion and this is Monk, and now we’re going to warm up for the performance.
